_note: Unit concepts for the 1805-09 slice: the shared families every European-drilled army uses, then each slice nation's distinctive units. Ratings are relative 1-5 in the provisional vocabulary (3 = ordinary line unit of 1805). 'art.asset' is the manifest id the unit is drawn with; status says whether that art exists. Recruitment and AI text is requirement, not implementation.

units.name: Line infantry
units.historical_basis: The musket-and-bayonet battalion of every European-drilled army.
units.role: Holds the line, delivers volleys, takes and keeps ground.
units.recruitment: Any barracks. The cheapest unit that can stand in open battle.
units.ai_use: The default garrison and battle line; keep adjacent to another friendly unit.

art.status: delivered (French look); other national looks planned

units.name: Light infantry
units.historical_basis: Skirmishers fighting in open order ahead of the line: voltigeurs, Jäger, light companies.
units.equipment: Musket, sometimes a shorter fusil; no formed bayonet charge.
units.role: Screens, harasses, fights in woods and broken ground.
units.recruitment: Barracks, after a first battle has been fought.
units.ai_use: Place in forest or rough hexes in front of the line; never leave alone in the open against cavalry.

units.name: Light cavalry
units.historical_basis: Hussars, chasseurs, light dragoons: scouting, pursuit and raiding.
units.role: Finds the enemy, runs down broken units, cuts supply.
units.recruitment: Stables. Limited by horses, not men.
units.ai_use: Send round the flank to attack artillery and retreating units; do not charge formed infantry frontally.

units.name: Heavy cavalry
units.historical_basis: Big men on big horses kept for the decisive charge: cuirassiers, heavy dragoons.
units.equipment: Straight sword; breastplate in some services.
units.role: Breaks a shaken line.
units.recruitment: Stables level 2. Slow to replace.
units.ai_use: Hold in reserve until an enemy unit is damaged, then charge it.

units.name: Foot artillery
units.historical_basis: Field batteries of 6- to 12-pounders moved by horse teams with gunners on foot.
units.equipment: Bronze smoothbore guns; roundshot and canister.
units.role: Wears down the enemy before the assault; defends against it with canister.
units.recruitment: Factory or arsenal.
units.ai_use: Deploy behind the infantry line with a clear field; retreat it first.

units.name: Ship of the line
units.historical_basis: The two-decked 74 and its larger cousins: the unit of sea power.
units.equipment: Sixty to over a hundred guns on two or three decks.
units.role: Wins and holds command of a sea zone; blockades.
units.recruitment: Port level 2 with a dockyard. Takes several turns.
units.ai_use: Keep in squadrons; blockade enemy ports.

units.name: Frigate
units.historical_basis: Single-decked cruisers for scouting, convoy and commerce war.
units.role: Raids and protects trade; scouts for the battle fleet.
units.recruitment: Any port.
units.ai_use: Send singly to trade lanes; avoid ships of the line.

units.name: Transport
units.historical_basis: Hired merchantmen carrying troops.
units.role: Moves land units by sea.
units.recruitment: Any port; cheap.
units.ai_use: Move only with an escort or across a controlled sea zone.

units.name: Militia
units.historical_basis: Part-time local forces: Landwehr, National Guard, provincial levies.
units.role: Garrisons towns so that regulars can march.
units.recruitment: Any city. May not leave home territory.
units.ai_use: Garrison only.

units.name: Grenadiers à pied de la Garde
units.historical_basis: The senior regiment of the Imperial Guard, chosen from veterans of long service and kept as the army's last reserve.
units.equipment: Musket and bayonet, short sabre; bearskin cap with brass plate.
units.role: Reserve that does not break; commits last and decides the day.
units.recruitment: Capital only, and only after a set number of victories. One at a time.
units.ai_use: Keep with the army commander; commit when a friendly line unit is about to rout or an enemy one is.

units.name: Chasseurs à cheval
units.historical_basis: The most numerous French light cavalry, in green, serving with every corps.
units.role: Corps cavalry: screen and pursuit.
units.recruitment: Stables.
units.ai_use: As light cavalry; attach one to each army.
units.note: France's instance of the shared light-cavalry family; same ratings by design.

units.name: Cuirassiers
units.historical_basis: Twelve regiments armoured in 1802-04 and massed in a reserve under Murat.
units.equipment: Straight sword, steel cuirass and helmet.
units.role: The battle-winning charge.
units.recruitment: Stables level 2 in France proper.
units.ai_use: Mass two or more and charge a damaged unit together.

units.name: Artillerie à cheval
units.historical_basis: Light guns with every gunner mounted, able to keep pace with cavalry.
units.role: Brings guns to the point of decision quickly.
units.recruitment: Arsenal and stables.
units.ai_use: Move with the cavalry reserve; unlimber adjacent to the unit about to be charged.

units.name: Royal Navy 74
units.historical_basis: The standard British battleship, with crews kept at sea and at gun drill by years of blockade.
units.equipment: Seventy-four guns; carronades on the upper works.
units.role: As ship of the line, with faster and more accurate fire.
units.recruitment: Royal dockyards (Portsmouth, Plymouth, Chatham).
units.ai_use: Blockade; accept battle at any odds short of two to one.

units.name: 95th Rifles
units.historical_basis: The Experimental Corps of Riflemen of 1800, the 95th from 1803: green-jacketed marksmen with the Baker rifle.
units.role: Long-range skirmisher that picks off officers and gunners.
units.recruitment: Britain only; few at a time.
units.ai_use: Place in cover ahead of the line; target artillery and commanders.
units.note: Slow to load: proposed as high fire at range 4, reduced fire when attacked at close quarters.

units.name: King's German Legion
units.historical_basis: Hanoverian soldiers who escaped the French occupation of 1803 and served Britain as a complete corps of all arms.
units.role: Regular troops Britain can raise without British manpower.
units.recruitment: Britain, while Hanover is occupied by an enemy.
units.ai_use: As line infantry.

units.name: Don Cossacks
units.historical_basis: Irregular hosts owing military service to the Tsar, each man with his own horses.
units.equipment: Lance, sabre, pistol; no uniform drill.
units.role: Scouts, raiders and pursuers; a screen no enemy cavalry can pin.
units.recruitment: Russian home territory; nearly free.
units.ai_use: Attach to every army; raid enemy supply; never stand against formed troops.

units.name: Pavlovsk Grenadiers
units.historical_basis: A grenadier regiment that kept the brass-fronted mitre cap of the previous century.
units.role: Assault infantry that takes losses and keeps coming.
units.recruitment: Saint Petersburg or Moscow.
units.ai_use: Lead assaults on towns and fortified hexes.

units.name: Licorne battery
units.historical_basis: The Russian 'unicorn', a long howitzer firing shell on a flatter path than other howitzers.
units.role: Artillery that reaches over friendly troops and into cover.
units.recruitment: Russian arsenals.
units.ai_use: As foot artillery; prefer targets in towns and woods.

units.name: Janissaries
units.historical_basis: The old standing infantry of the sultans, by 1805 a hereditary corporation of armed townsmen that resisted drill and reform.
units.equipment: Long musket, yataghan; no bayonet, no formed manoeuvre.
units.role: Formidable behind walls and in a rush; unreliable in open battle.
units.recruitment: Present from the start in every fortress; cannot be raised anew.
units.ai_use: Garrison fortresses; in the field use for assaults, not for holding a line.
units.note: Upkeep is paid whether or not they fight; disbanding them is the reform track's final step.

units.name: Nizam-ı Cedid infantry
units.historical_basis: Selim III's 'New Order' corps, drilled and dressed on European lines.
units.role: A modern line unit for an army that has few.
units.recruitment: Constantinople and Anatolian depots; each new unit costs stability until reform is complete.
units.ai_use: As line infantry; keep near the capital while stability is low.

units.name: Sipahi cavalry
units.historical_basis: Provincial cavalry holding land in return for service.
units.equipment: Sabre, lance, firearms of their own choosing.
units.role: Numerous medium horse.
units.recruitment: Any Ottoman province.
units.ai_use: Use in mass on the flanks.

units.name: Deli light horse
units.historical_basis: Balkan irregular horsemen famous for reckless charges, hired by provincial governors.
units.role: Shock raiders: a fierce first charge and nothing after it.
units.recruitment: Balkan provinces; cheap.
units.ai_use: Charge once at a damaged unit, then withdraw.

units.name: Banner cavalry
units.historical_basis: Hereditary Manchu and Mongol soldiers of the Eight Banners, by training mounted archers.
units.role: Mounted archery: mobile fire without closing.
units.recruitment: Beijing, Mukden and banner garrison cities; capped by banner households.
units.ai_use: Shoot and withdraw; close only against broken units.

units.name: Green Standard infantry
units.historical_basis: The Han Chinese regular army, most of it dispersed in small posts as a constabulary.
units.role: Numerous garrison infantry.
units.recruitment: Any Qing province; cheap and slow to concentrate.
units.ai_use: Garrison; in battle use numbers, two units to one.

units.name: Rattan-shield troops
units.historical_basis: Shock infantry in striped 'tiger' dress with rattan shields, trained to close under fire.
units.role: Close-assault infantry against irregulars and rebels.
units.recruitment: Southern provinces.
units.ai_use: Assault rebel-held hexes; keep away from artillery.

units.name: War junk
units.historical_basis: Coastal fighting junks of the provincial fleets.
units.equipment: A few small guns, boarding crews.
units.role: Coastal defence and anti-piracy.
units.recruitment: Guangzhou, Xiamen and river ports.
units.ai_use: Stay in coastal zones under shore batteries.

units.name: Silladar horse
units.historical_basis: Cavalrymen who own their horses and arms and serve under contract to a chief.
units.role: Fast-moving light horse for raids and envelopment.
units.recruitment: Any Maratha house.
units.ai_use: Avoid infantry squares; go for the baggage and the guns' flanks.

units.name: Pindari raiders
units.historical_basis: Unpaid irregular horsemen attached to Maratha armies and living by plunder.
units.role: Devastation: destroys an enemy province's income.
units.recruitment: Free; appears while a Maratha army is in enemy territory.
units.ai_use: Never fight; raid undefended revenue provinces.
units.note: Proposed new mechanic: 'raid' action that removes income instead of dealing damage.

units.name: Campoo infantry
units.historical_basis: Scindia's brigades drilled by de Boigne and Perron, with their own foundries; broken at Assaye and Laswari in 1803.
units.equipment: Flintlock musket and bayonet, excellent artillery train.
units.role: A regular line the Company must respect.
units.recruitment: Not available at the start. Needs foreign officers: a French relation above neutral or captured Company stores.
units.ai_use: As line infantry with artillery support.

units.name: Heavy frigate
units.historical_basis: Joshua Humphreys' 44s (Constitution, United States, President): frigates built with a battleship's scantlings.
units.equipment: Thirty 24-pounders on the gun deck, carronades above.
units.role: Beats any frigate, outruns any ship of the line.
units.recruitment: Boston, Philadelphia, Norfolk; an act of Congress each.
units.ai_use: Cruise alone against trade and lone frigates; refuse squadron battle.

units.name: Frontier riflemen
units.historical_basis: Volunteer riflemen of Kentucky, Tennessee and the Ohio country with the long rifle.
units.equipment: American long rifle; tomahawk; no bayonet.
units.role: Accurate fire from cover; cannot stand a charge.
units.recruitment: Western states and territories.
units.ai_use: Defend woods and field works; retreat from open ground.

units.name: State militia
units.historical_basis: The enrolled militia of the states, called out for short terms.
units.role: Defends its own state.
units.recruitment: Any state; may not cross the frontier.
units.ai_use: Garrison.
units.note: America's instance of the shared militia family.

units.name: Armée indigène infantry
units.historical_basis: The army that defeated Leclerc's expedition: demi-brigades of veterans formed in the colonial and revolutionary wars.
units.equipment: French-pattern musket and bayonet; uniforms as supply allows.
units.role: Veteran line infantry that fights best in hills and on the defence.
units.recruitment: Available at the start; replacements arrive as ordinary line infantry.
units.ai_use: Defend rough terrain and forts; counter-attack an invader weakened by fever.

units.name: Mountain fort
units.historical_basis: The chain of interior forts ordered by Dessalines in 1805, crowned by Christophe's Citadelle.
units.equipment: Masonry works on ridges, heavy guns, cisterns and magazines.
units.role: A refuge the army can hold for a year.
units.recruitment: Mountain hexes only.
units.ai_use: Hold; never abandon while supplied.

units.name: Jihadist archers
units.historical_basis: The foot of the Shehu's community: Fulani and Hausa bowmen who won at Tabkin Kwotto fighting in a square.
units.role: Steady missile infantry that fights for the cause.
units.recruitment: Arrives with each victory; leaves after a defeat.
units.ai_use: Form on rough or wooded ground and let cavalry come.

units.name: Emirate cavalry
units.historical_basis: Horsemen in quilted armour of the kind the Hausa kingdoms fielded, brought over or captured as the emirates fell.
units.equipment: Lance, sword, quilted cotton armour for man and horse.
units.role: The heavy cavalry the movement lacks at the start.
units.recruitment: Only from a conquered Hausa capital or an emirate.
units.ai_use: Charge enemy archers and infantry in the open.
